key_insight: Multimodal MoE models can accurately perceive visual content but fail at downstream reasoning because expert routing distracts reasoning pathways; the problem is not lack of cross-modal semantic sharing but routing behavior that misroutes visual signals.
problem_solved: Explains and fixes the paradox where vision-language MoE models "see" images correctly yet "don't think" about them — i.e., a perception-to-reasoning gap caused by routing distraction in the mixture-of-experts architecture.
method: Systematic diagnosis: measure perception vs. reasoning performance on matched image and text problems and probe cross-modal semantic sharing to rule out alignment failure.
Routing analysis: inspect gating decisions and token-to-expert flows to identify ‘routing distraction’ — visual tokens routed to experts that impede reasoning.
Mitigation proposals: introduce routing-aware interventions (e.g., routing regularization, expert specialization or auxiliary reasoning losses) and ablations to restore correct reasoning behavior.
impact: Helps practitioners diagnose and remedy a critical failure mode in multimodal MoEs, improving robustness and interpretability of vision-language systems and guiding design of gating/routing mechanisms for reliable multimodal reasoning.
visual_elements: Schematic of a multimodal MoE showing token routing arrows: correct vs. distracted routing (color-coded).
Side-by-side example: same problem presented with image vs. text, showing perception OK but reasoning failure for the image case.
Sankey/heatmap of routing probabilities across experts illustrating concentration of visual tokens into distracting experts.
Bar chart/ablation table: accuracy gap (perception vs. reasoning) before and after routing-aware mitigations.
paper_title: Seeing but Not Thinking: Routing Distraction in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Haolei Xu, Haiwen Hong, Hongxing Li, Rui Zhou, Yang Zhang
